notes: Prices are STANDARD list rates. Promotional or introductory rates are
deliberately NOT used: cost ceilings exist to protect the operator, so
estimation must never under-report. Claude Sonnet 5 carries an
introductory rate of 2.00/10.00 through 2026-08-31; the standard
3.00/15.00 is recorded here so ceilings trigger conservatively.
Regional multipliers (US-only inference is 1.1x) and Batch API (-50%)
and prompt caching (-90% on cached input) are NOT applied here. Those
are applied by the client at estimation time when the relevant option
is in use, again only where doing so cannot under-report.
charsPerTokenConservative is deliberately LOW. Fewer characters per
token means more tokens estimated, means higher estimated cost, means
the ceiling engages earlier. Typical French and English prose runs
roughly 3.5-4.0 chars/token on the v1 tokenizer; the v2 tokenizer
(Opus 4.7 and later) can emit up to 35 percent more tokens for the
same input. 2.6 is chosen to stay conservative across both.
This value is a SAFE PLACEHOLDER, not a calibrated measurement.
Design doc risk 6.5-Risk-7 calls for benchmarking before migration;
until that benchmark exists, erring high is the correct posture.
unknownModelFallback: if a configured model is absent from the table
below, price it as the most expensive current model rather than
refusing the call or assuming it is cheap. An unrecognised model must
never estimate lower than a recognised one.

legacyRetentionPolicy.reason: Requirement 6.5-R13. Deployed field configurations reference these model identifiers; removing them from this table would cause the client to reject a working production configuration. Legacy entries are retained with accurate pricing so that existing deployments keep correct cost estimation, and are marked status=legacy so tooling can surface an upgrade recommendation without forcing one.
